wellbeing.satisfactionCompositionDescription: Each axis average multiplied by its weight, stacked. The stack height is the household satisfaction score.
wellbeing.comfortCompositionDescription: The four factors' contributions, stacked. The housing-adequacy multiplier is already applied, so the stack height equals living comfort.
wellbeing.leisureDescription: Free time and working hours use the right axis; leisure and satisfaction use the left. Less time reduces leisure spending.
wellbeing.workDescription: Labor output scales with an 8-hour baseline. Longer hours reduce leisure; sustained work above 8 hours harms health. Applies from the next simulation.
wellbeing.desc_satis_wealth: Driven by the goods households actually managed to buy — clothing, processed food, appliances, jewelry — not by income.
wellbeing.desc_satis_leisure: Driven by the services households used: dining, entertainment, beauty, telecom. Long commutes and work hours cut free time, and spending with it.
wellbeing.desc_satis_health: The household average of citizen health. Poor nutrition, bad sanitation, air pollution and overwork lower it; medical services restore it.
wellbeing.desc_satis_comfort: The average of housing space, quietness, sunlight and safety, multiplied by housing adequacy. Cramped housing caps the rest.
wellbeing.desc_satisfaction: The weighted total of the four axes. City-score accident penalties are excluded.
wellbeing.desc_satis_residential: The floor area of the household's home divided by what it needs. Meeting the need is 100%, which is also the display ceiling.
wellbeing.desc_quiet: The inverse of noise on the home's parcel. Nearby trunk roads, railways and factories lower it.
wellbeing.desc_sunlight: Sunlight on the home's parcel. The longer it sits in shadow, the lower it gets.
wellbeing.desc_safety: The inverse of crime risk on the home's parcel. Crime-prone locations lower it.
